summary: Translate tawro as ox instead of cow
rationale: The Turoyo lu tawrayḏan refers to an ox, and the supplied edition translation at 44/95 explicitly reads Unser Ochse hat sich erholt. The supplied Ritter dictionary defines tawro as Stier, Ochse and cites 44/86 ff. Cow incorrectly makes the animal female.

summary: Correct both identifications of the animal: cow → ox
before: My uncle took off his pants and I wrapped them over it (the cow, m) little by little and God healed it (the cow, m) up
after: My uncle took off his pants and I wrapped them over it (the ox, m) little by little and God healed it (the ox, m) up
rationale: Both parenthetical identifications refer to the same ox. The edition at 44/113 says dem Ochsen; 44/94 explicitly identifies the animal as u tawro, and the supplied Ritter dictionary defines tawro as Stier, Ochse. Both occurrences of cow contradict this identification and the annotation m.
